title: Technical English — Course 5, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 4

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the fault-analysis class take place?
tasks.audioText: The engineering analysis class will review a case involving an intermittent equipment indication on Tuesday at nine. Students should bring the event log and the maintenance history extract. The tutor will ask groups to build a timeline, identify what is confirmed and list possible explanations that still require evidence. The class will not diagnose live equipment.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which two records should students bring?
tasks.audioText: The engineering analysis class will review a case involving an intermittent equipment indication on Tuesday at nine. Students should bring the event log and the maintenance history extract. The tutor will ask groups to build a timeline, identify what is confirmed and list possible explanations that still require evidence. The class will not diagnose live equipment.
options: The event log and maintenance history extract

tasks.prompt: A fault-analysis team reviewed an intermittent indication reported on several occasions. The event log showed when the indication appeared, while the maintenance history identified earlier work on the system. The team compared the timing of events but did not assume that the earlier work caused the problem. Further evidence was required before the team could confirm a cause or recommend a corrective action. Reading 1. What did the event log show?
Why did the team avoid linking the earlier work directly to the problem?
options: Further evidence was required before confirming a cause

tasks.prompt: The possible relationship ___ before a cause is confirmed.
Choose TWO records that may support fault analysis.
A sequence of events arranged by date and time is a ___.
A colleague says that earlier maintenance definitely caused the fault, but evidence is incomplete. What should you say?
options: The timing may be relevant, but we need further evidence before confirming a causal link.
We should remove the event log.
The conclusion does not need support.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of integrated fault analysis in a logical order.
options: Compare the records and identify gaps
Build a timeline from the event log
State possible explanations and evidence still required
correctOrder: Build a timeline from the event log
Compare the records and identify gaps
State possible explanations and evidence still required

tasks.prompt: Write 100–120 words summarising an intermittent fault investigation. Separate the timeline, confirmed facts, possible explanations and evidence still needed.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: task completion and relevant content (0–2); clear organisation and logical linking (0–2); grammar and sentence structure (0–2); precise technical vocabulary, spelling and punctuation (0–2). Minor errors are acceptable if meaning remains clear.
